items.note: Twenty novices co-wrote cartoon captions with an NLP incongruity tool and 66 separate raters judged them funnier than captions written without the tool; the next stage should check whether the tool is generative AI and how the no-tool captions were produced.

Within-subjects study with 12 designers comparing a structured multi-phase prompt-based design tool with a conversational generative-AI baseline; prompt diversity rose and image diversity was comparable (AI-configuration contrast, small sample).

Randomized LLM-use policy for ICML 2026 reviewers with outcomes on paper decisions, scores, confidence, and review length; peer review is not a creative task and no creativity or diversity outcome is scored.

Within-subject study comparing Reverger, an AI story-ideation tool scaffolding divergence and convergence, with a comparable AI baseline; participants explored more unexpected and diverse directions (sample size not in the abstract; unclear whether diversity is scored or self-reported).

Comparative study (N=24) of AtoMix, an atomic-prompting GenAI interface for remote 6-3-5 visual brainwriting, against a baseline (likely GenAI-embedded brainwriting); a formative study (N=18) reported redundancy and limited divergence with GenAI.

User study with 10 fashion designers comparing CLAY, a text-to-image tool for managing prompt vagueness, with their existing practice; reported outcomes (design time, creative possibilities) may be self-reported only, which the next stage should check.

System paper on Amuse, a multimodal-LLM chord-suggestion assistant for songwriters; the user study states no comparison condition and reports agency and creativity in the process, so the next stage could confirm whether the full text has a baseline arm.

Within-subject study with 16 professional UX designers doing one UI task without AI and one with FigmaAI; AI-assisted designs were more visually and structurally similar (diversity outcome; order randomization not stated).

Book chapter comparing design ideation sessions assisted by ALIA, a speech-based analogical LLM agent, with traditional sessions; preliminary results rest on participants' self-ratings, and this is likely an earlier report of the study in c816 (doi 10.1017/dsj.2025.10044).

Controlled ideation experiments with 24 undergraduate design students where groups assisted by an LLM analogical-stimuli tool generated higher-rated ideas than unassisted groups, plus an LLM benchmark; same tool (ALIA) and likely same study as c815.
